questions.stem: In a reaction, 0.1 mol of zinc reacts with 0.04 mol of hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Which is the limiting reactant?

options.text: Zinc, because it has fewer moles
Zinc, because it has a higher Mr
Hydrochloric acid, because 0.1 mol Zn would need 0.2 mol HCl but only 0.04 mol is available
Neither, because they react in equal amounts

questions.explanation: From the equation, 1 mol Zn requires 2 mol HCl. So 0.1 mol Zn would need 0.2 mol HCl. Only 0.04 mol HCl is available, so HCl runs out first and is the limiting reactant. The amount of product is determined by the limiting reactant.

questions.stem: What is meant by the term 'limiting reactant'?

options.text: The reactant with the largest mass
The reactant that is completely used up and determines the amount of product formed
The reactant that is left over at the end of a reaction
The reactant with the smallest Mr

questions.explanation: The limiting reactant is the one that is completely used up first in a reaction. It limits (determines) the maximum amount of product that can be formed. The other reactant(s) are said to be 'in excess' because some will be left over.
